Markus / Neha / Priya — quick legal note and suggested compromise language below. I kept it narrow to avoid reopening broader MSA economics.

1) Governing law: Our standard is Delaware. If Northshore will not accept Delaware, we can agree New York as a second choice. We should avoid agreeing to California law as a general policy.

2) Injunctive relief carveout: the typical workable compromise is: 

"Notwithstanding the Agreement's arbitration provision, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction located in: (a) the State of Delaware; or (b) the State in which the party seeking relief maintains its principal place of business. The foregoing shall not be construed to waive the parties' agreement to arbitrate any dispute not involving provisional equitable relief."

This keeps arbitration for the merits while allowing immediate court relief for preservation matters. If Northshore insists on CA-only courts for emergency relief, we can accept 'State in which the party seeking relief maintains its principal place of business' to capture CA for them.

3) Practical: add an expedited preservation notice process (48 hours) before injunctive filings where feasible and include a covenant not to use injunctive relief to bypass arbitration on the merits. That language helps limit abuse.

If you want, I'll paste this snippet into the order form redline and re-run. I'm fine with New York if that's the customer's preference over Delaware.

Attachment: redline_snippet.txt (proposed sentence for Order Form)

—Laura
